answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because signal only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, pearl is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
